sources.name: Los Angeles Police Department criminal homicide, 2010-2023
sources.notes: City of Los Angeles only (LAPD area, about 40% of the county's people). Two frozen sets, Crime Data from 2010 to 2019 (63jg-8b9z) and from 2020 to Present (2nrs-mtv8), criminal homicide (Crm Cd 110) only, 2024 left out (incomplete in the source). Locations are the source's hundred-block points snapped to the 1 km grid; only counts per cell, year and homicide/firearm are kept, no victim age, sex or descent. sources.name: Cincinnati Police murders, 2011-
sources.notes: Two files in a row: the old RMS file k59e-2pvf to 2024-06-02 and the new STARS-category file 7aqy-xrv9 from 2024-06-03 (the city changed record systems). Offenses counted: murder, aggravated murder (and its felony/premeditated variants) and voluntary manslaughter; involuntary manslaughter, reckless and negligent homicide are left out. The old file repeats each incident several times with coordinates jittered by a few metres (same instanceid), so it is counted once per instanceid. 2010 is a part-year (27,488 records against 49,017 in 2011) and is left out. 18% of the rows have no coordinates in the source and are not on the map. No weapon field in the new file, so no firearm split. Only date and coordinates are requested; no victim age or sex. Preview built 2026-10-10; approved by the owner in chat 2026-10-10 (live in the repo copy, not pushed).

sources.name: Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police homicide victims, 2015-
sources.notes: UCR murder and non-negligent manslaughter victims in the CMPD jurisdiction, January 2015 to date (1,059 victims, one request, no paging). Year is the year reported (CALENDAR_YEAR matches DATE_REPORTED in every row). Firearm = the weapon field names a handgun, rifle, shotgun or firearm. The public coordinates are snapped to the 1 km grid; only date, weapon and coordinates are requested (no age, sex, race, circumstances or clearance). Yearly counts run 60-118 and sit within about 10% of the CDC county figures for Mecklenburg (2019 102 vs 104-126). Preview built 2026-10-10; approved by the owner in chat 2026-10-10 (live in the repo copy, not pushed).

sources.name: Atlanta Police Department homicides, 1997-
sources.notes: Three APD files in a row (ArcGIS services under services3.arcgis.com/Et5Qfajgiyosiw4d): Crime_Data_1997_2008 (UCR code 110 'homicide'; negligent manslaughter 120 left out), 2009_2020CrimeData (APD's own HOMICIDE crime type, whose local codes 901-912 the portal does not define, so a few non-murder records may be included; no weapon field) and OpenDataWebsite_Crime_view (NIBRS 09A, 2021-, one count per victim: 157, 171, 136, 125, 100 for 2021-2025). Year is the year the offence occurred. City of Atlanta only (Fulton County has more). Only year, date and coordinates are requested. The portal's robots.txt (opendata.atlantapd.org) asks for a 60-second crawl delay; only three requests went to that host (robots.txt, the catalog feed and the home page, a few minutes apart, so closer than 60 s) and every data request went to the ArcGIS service host instead. Preview built 2026-10-10; approved by the owner in chat 2026-10-10 (live in the repo copy, not pushed).

sources.name: Denver Police murders, 2021-
sources.notes: NIBRS offenses file (ODC_CRIME_OFFENSES_P, the previous five calendar years plus the current year to date). Category 'murder', types homicide-family (0902) and homicide-other (0912), one count per victim (VICTIM_COUNT). Negligent homicide (0910) and police killings by gun (0907, in the police-killings layer) left out. 375 victims 2021-2026; 2021 84 and 2025 39 against CDC deaths-in-Denver 85 and 40. The catalog also lists annual CSVs for 2010-2021 (large downloads, not fetched; a file download needs the owner's yes). Locations are approximate by the publisher. Preview built 2026-10-10; approved by the owner in chat 2026-10-10 (live in the repo copy, not pushed).

sources.notes: PDFs in sources/il_idph/. Agreement 100% (suicide 341 checked, homicide 158); about 1,501 fills (suicide 947, homicide 554). Accidents and all-injury sections are in the bundle but have no MortalGIS measure.

sources.name: Indiana ISDH annual Mortality Report, tables 5 and 9 by county
sources.notes: Raw pages: sources/in_isdh_mortality_report_tables5_9_2000-2017_html.zip. Agreement 99.5-100% (Table 5), falls 97.7%, suicide 99.7%, homicide 100% (Table 9). About 5,366 + 728 (Table 5, 2003-2017 and 2000-2002) and 2,013 + 197 (Table 9) fills. Merge the 2000-2002 file with the 2003-2017 file per cause before the build, otherwise the 50-county-year agreement check fails for the small causes. 2014 Wayne page missing on the site. No Table 5 edition after 2017 at this address.

sources.name: Tennessee Department of Health deaths by county (annual PDFs 2009-2017, Excel 2018-2022)
sources.notes: 116 originals plus the release policy PDF in sources/tn_health/ (one link, AccidentDeaths_County_2022.xlsx, is a 404 on TN's own page). Agreement 98.5-100%; about 1,909 fills. Accidents and motor-vehicle tables are in the bundle but have no MortalGIS measure. A 2014-2017 four-year county workbook (LCD-AllCounties2014-17.xlsx, about 30 causes) is saved but not parsed.

sources.name: Wisconsin WISH mortality module, broad causes by county of residence
sources.notes: Query-result pages saved verbatim in sources/wi_wish/. Agreement 98.6-100%; about 3,291 exact fills (homicide has only 47 checked county-years, so the 50-cell gate skips it; 100% agreement on those). Plus about 4,342 CDC-hidden cells where WISH masks only 1-4, so they can show 1-4 instead of 1-9 (bundle key `masked`; not wired). FLAG: 2014 disagrees with CDC in 15-25% of county-years in every cause while other years disagree 0-3% (CDC and WISH differ on 2014 county assignment); the build gate skips 2014 only for Alzheimer's, CLRD, heart and stroke, so skip 2014 for WI altogether.

sources.name: Missouri MICA (Death MICA), county by cause by year
sources.notes: MICA hides whole county rows when one cell is 1-4, so it is pulled one cause and one year at a time (499 queries, 20 cause definitions). Raw per-query results: sources/mo_mica/mo_mica_death_county_year_raw.json. Agreement 98.3-100% for 13 causes and 93.6% for overdose (three low years, 2001, 2004 and 2007, are skipped by the build rule); about 6,631 unique exact fills (suicide 641, homicide 169, liver 435, kidney 874, flu 874, Alzheimer's 766, diabetes 862, CLRD 629, stroke 717, COVID 85, firearm 138, overdose 430, cancer 45, heart 43). Falls fail the check (83% agreement; MICA's Falls node is not the CDC definition) and are not usable. Plus about 10,500 CDC-hidden cells that MICA shows as x in tables where every x is a true 1-4 (bundle key `narrow_1_4`), so they could show 1-4 instead of 1-9. x cells from tables with 1-5 x rows can include complementary-suppressed larger values and are NOT narrowed. St. Louis city and county are both named St. Louis in CDC's list; the bundle carries `fips_alias`. The Confidentiality page does not mention the x symbol; the rule was verified on the data (min shown count 5, explicit zeros shown, x rows consistent with state totals).

sources.name: Florida CHARTS deaths by county (113 selected causes)
sources.notes: Raw query text dumps (128 causes x 67 counties x 1970-2024) in scratch_crawl/fl_raw/*.txt, packaged in staging/fl_charts_county_1970-2024.json. Verified 2026-10-09: three causes re-parsed from the raw dumps match the bundle; the live FLHealthCHARTS site was not re-queried. Against CDC (1999-2024 overlap): 12,165 county-years checked, 98.0% within tolerance, 77% of CDC counts of 10-19 reproduced exactly (falls 76%, stroke 70%, homicide 73%, suicide 73% fall below the 80% warning line). Low-agreement years are skipped by the build rule. 6,315 exact fills if approved (homicide 1,907, suicide 1,405, firearm 1,408, falls 688, stroke 538, diabetes 365, cancer 4); the bundle holds seven populated causes (Alzheimer's and COVID are empty in it; all-deaths, heart, CLRD and the rest were not pulled). Three state-years are off the WONDER total (year 2000, 2-7% over). Accidental poisoning (X40-X49) is separate from CDC all-intent poisoning, so overdose was not used. Earlier note (2,423 fills, agreement 94.2-96.3%) was from the old snapshot and is superseded.

sources.name: Maryland Department of Health Vital Statistics Administration Annual Reports (Table 48/43)
sources.notes: Annual report PDFs 1996-2024 in scratch_crawl/md_raw/; Table 48 (43 in 2021-2024) parsed by staging/scripts/md_parse.py, which hard-codes page numbers and column positions, so re-check it each year. Verified 2026-10-09: a 2022 spot-check of the bundle against the PDF is clean. Against CDC: 3,132 county-years checked, 97.9% within tolerance, 66% of CDC counts of 10-19 reproduced exactly (homicide 53%, stroke 52%, suicide 74%; homicide 92.0% and suicide 94.5% agreement sit under 95%). 582 exact fills if approved (homicide 343, suicide 214, COVID 16, stroke 9). All-deaths, cancer and heart have no hidden cells in CDC's Maryland data (0 of 624 county-years), so they fill nothing. Motor vehicle has no CDC measure. 9 of 161 state-years are off the WONDER total (up to 10% short). Baltimore City (24510) and Baltimore County (24005) resolved via fips_alias. Earlier note (163 fills) was from the old snapshot and is superseded.

sources.name: Alabama DPH Center for Health Statistics 113 Selected Causes of Death by County of Residence
sources.notes: Annual '113 Selected Causes of Death by County of Residence, Race and Sex' PDFs in scratch_crawl/al_raw/. Only 2015-2024 are real files (about 285 pages each); 13 of the 1999-2014 downloads are identical 39,250-byte error pages and nothing before 2015 was read. Parsed by staging/scripts/al_parse.py. Verified 2026-10-09: 1,608 bundle values re-parsed from the PDFs match. Against CDC: 3,471 county-years checked, 100% within tolerance, 95% of CDC counts of 10-19 reproduced exactly. 1,350 exact fills if approved, all 2019-2024 (homicide 304, suicide 229, liver 204, kidney 202, diabetes 142, COVID 89, Alzheimer's 86, CLRD 54, stroke 40). FIREARM IS SKIP: the bundle holds zeros for 2015-2018 (cause not traced), agreement is 61% and four state-years sit 100% under WONDER; its 215 fills are not used. Earlier note (748 fills, firearm 215 counted) is superseded.

sources.name: Georgia DPH OASIS Mortality Data Table Tool
sources.notes: Automated pull (staging/scripts/ga_oasis_pull.js) of the OASIS mortality table tool's JSON endpoint, 159 counties x 1999-2024. Verified 2026-10-09: re-pulled from the live site and matches the bundle. Against CDC: 25,506 county-years checked, 94.3% within tolerance (cause range about 90-97%: flu/pneumonia 90.1%, homicide 90.6%, heart 92.3%, cancer 93.4%), and only 52% of CDC counts of 10-19 reproduced exactly (cause range 37-62%). So GA's small counts are typically right to within a few deaths, not exact. 23,442 exact fills if approved, about 60% of everything the six new sources add. 61 of 343 comparable state-years are off the WONDER total (median 2.7% short; flu/pneumonia 1999 and 2000 are 35% and 20% short). Motor vehicle has no CDC measure. Treat as the source to review first: consider approving cause by cause, or not at all. Earlier note (1,181 fills; heart and stroke 100% agreement) was from the old snapshot and is superseded.

sources.name: South Carolina DPH SCAN Mortality Query System
sources.notes: Automated pull (staging/scripts/sc_scan_pull.js) of the SCAN ASP.NET table generator, 46 counties x 1999-2024. Verified 2026-10-09: re-pulled from the live site and matches the bundle. Against CDC: 9,984 county-years checked, 99.7% within tolerance, 91% of CDC counts of 10-19 reproduced exactly. 2,090 exact fills if approved (homicide 299, suicide 249, kidney 301, flu/pneumonia 295, liver 285, diabetes 223, Alzheimer's 212, CLRD 124, stroke 76, COVID 26) plus 1,912 cells where CDC shows 1-9 and SCAN shows only that the count is under 5 (1-4 band, not wired into the map). The '#' mask means under 5. No state-year is off the WONDER total (319 compared). SC's 'Unknown' county row (364 bundle rows) is not assigned to a county. Earlier note (153 fills) was from the old snapshot and is superseded.

sources.name: Mississippi State Department of Health MSTAHRS Mortality Query Tool
sources.notes: Automated pull (staging/scripts/ms_mstahrs_pull.js) of the MSTAHRS query tool, 82 counties x 1999-2024 (homicide ends 2022; the publisher holds 2023-2024). Verified 2026-10-09: re-pulled from the live site and matches the bundle. Against CDC: 13,084 county-years checked, 99.8% within tolerance, 91% of CDC counts of 10-19 reproduced exactly (homicide 75% is under the 80% warning line). 4,987 exact fills if approved (flu/pneumonia 694, kidney 737, diabetes 638, Alzheimer's 485, suicide 422, stroke 433, liver 408, CLRD 416, homicide 365, falls 313, COVID 61, others fewer) plus 7,904 band cells (CDC 1-9 narrowed to 1-4; not wired into the map). OVERDOSE IS SKIP (65% agreement; 111 fills not used). Known data gaps: Alzheimer's 2023 and 2024 are about 95% under the WONDER total, and COVID 2018-2019 carries counts where WONDER has none. Motor vehicle has no CDC measure. Earlier note (199 fills) was from the old snapshot and is superseded.

sources.name: Oklahoma State Department of Health OK2SHARE detailed mortality (ICD-10, final trend form)
sources.notes: One query per year (2010-2024), rows county of residence by the 39-cause ICD-10 list, counts only, pulled 2026-10-10 UTC in headless Chrome after the agreement was accepted (terms_log/). Raw result pages and SHA-256 in sources/ok_ok2share/. Agreement 95.3-100% per cause; kidney 2022 and 2023 fall under 80% and the build skips them (OK2SHARE is lower than CDC in 2-4 counties a year, 2022-2024). About 2,119 unique exact fills, all counts of 5-9. Cancer, heart, falls, firearm and overdose are not in the 39-cause list (Oklahoma splits cancer and heart into parts); a 2019 test pull of the 113-cause list has falls only.

sources.name: Colorado CDPHE Vital Statistics, leading causes of death by county of residence, 2025
sources.notes: One xlsx (159,130 bytes, SHA-256 89f35887...), downloaded 2026-10-10 UTC with the owner's yes. Every county's listed causes plus 'Other' equal its All Causes row. One year only, so the build's 50-checked gate fails for every cause except all deaths (62 checked, 100%); the per-cause agreement is 83-100% (cancer, heart, CLRD, stroke, diabetes, COVID at 100%). Up to 165 CDC-hidden 2025 cells could fill (counts 3-9) if the owner approves cause by cause; 2025 is not yet in CDC's final data. Earlier years need the CoHID dashboard or a data request.

sources.name: New Jersey NJSHAD mortality count query (county of residence x cause, 2000-2024)

The table is a July 2017 run: Kansas sits 1-2 below CDC in most counties and well below in Kingman (102 vs 142), Greeley (15 vs 23) and Brown (111 vs 118); among the 47 fills the largest all-cause gaps to CDC are Greeley (KDHE 15 vs CDC 23; a cancer fill of 5) and Edwards (28 vs 32; cancer 3, heart 9), so those few values may read low.
